chapter: Looking back and the lean years
title: Segregation in Fort Lauderdale and Lake Tahoe with an integrated band
summary: At Fascio's Supper Club his Black sidemen face bomb threats and cannot find rooms, and at Lake Tahoe no one will house them.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Anyway, we got there and opened up and, of course, when Fascio took a look at the band and he

took me over to the side and he said - I didn't know you had any colored guys in the band -- I said, well, what's the difference? He said, well, Jesus, the colored people don't work together with white down here and I said - well, Christ, this is a hell of a time to tell me. I said, the booking office should have told me. He said, well, anyway, we'll do it without you. Well, the first couple of days he got bomb threats and people were going to burn the place down and such things as that. And, I couldn't find a place for the colored guys to live and now they wouldn't take them in the colored town; they wouldn't take the guys in the colored section because they were working with a white band. So, it worked in reverse you see.

We lost both ways. So, I drove them out on the highway - we were stopping in every motel for about 13 or 14 miles and I finally got a guy from Boston -- he said, oh, come on - let them live here, you know. This is a hell of a thing to happen and, so, we stayed there and I remember once I was standing in a washroom -- washing my hands -- and there was a couple guys standing there and they said - 'oh, Jesus, look -- here's that nigger lover now.' And, man, I mean I went flying out of there - and I mean some real bad guys, you know. And, so, we had that problem and I remember we went on - not from that particular job - we finished it up but on another occasion, I had taken almost that same group to Lake Tahoe

and not thinking that same kind of a thing prevailed in Lake Tahoe. I got there and we worked this club and no one would take my colored guys in. Nobody. They just wouldn't and somebody gave us a -- some kind person gave the colored guys in the band a filthy room with three beds in it -- fit for dogs you know, and I had that problem there. But at that time, you talk about having problems ---
What year would you say that was about? Was it soon after Condon?
Well it's in the time -- you know, I was out of Condon's for years but---
